video_identity.subject: Reference Image Setup in Blender 2.8 and PureRef Workflow for 3D Modeling

episodes.observed_visual_fact: The instructor opens Blender 2.8, deletes default scene objects, creates a cube, and uses Shift+A > Image > Reference while in Perspective View. The imported reference image plane aligns diagonally to the current viewport camera angle rather than an orthographic axis.
episodes.instructor_claim: Demonstrates the common mistake of importing reference images in perspective view, causing misaligned reference planes when rotating around objects.
episodes.interpretation: Importing a reference image plane while in standard perspective view locks its rotation vector to the active view camera orientation, rendering it unsuitable for orthographic tracing.
episodes.hypothesis: Blender's default behavior for 'Image as Reference' uses the view angle matrix at the time of creation to establish object rotation.
episodes.concrete_action: Press Shift+A -> Image -> Reference inside Perspective View.
episodes.reason: Illustrate a common alignment error during reference setup in Blender.
episodes.failure_or_warning: Importing reference planes in 3D perspective view creates an arbitrary angle aligned to the active viewport, causing misalignment during modeling.
episodes.transferable_principle: Avoid importing reference cards in free perspective view when orthographic alignment is required.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: The instructor switches to Front Orthographic view (Numpad 1), imports the reference image plane, scales it, duplicates it with Shift+D, rotates it 90 degrees on the Z-axis (R Z 90), and toggles Wireframe mode (Z) to show cross-plane reference modeling around a 3D primitive.
episodes.instructor_claim: Pressing 1 on the numpad puts you in front view straight on; importing reference here aligns it perfectly. Duplicating and rotating 90 degrees allows viewing references from all sides in wireframe mode.
episodes.interpretation: Aligning reference cards strictly to principal orthographic axes enables accurate multi-view bounding box matching when working in wireframe/x-ray modes.
episodes.hypothesis: A dual-card orthographic setup inside Blender improves proportion fidelity during initial blockout modeling.
episodes.concrete_action: Press Numpad 1, press Shift+A -> Image -> Reference, press Shift+D, press R Z 90, press Z to switch to Wireframe mode.
episodes.reason: Create an accurate orthographic cross-reference card setup within the 3D viewport.
episodes.transferable_principle: Always enter a locked orthographic view before importing reference image planes intended for direct 3D tracing.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: The instructor demonstrates PureRef software. He resizes the canvas, copies an image from Photoshop using Ctrl+C and pastes it into PureRef using Ctrl+V, toggles 'Always-on-Top' mode via Ctrl+Shift+A, crops an image using C + Left Click Drag, flips images using Alt+Shift+H and Alt+Shift+V, and opens the keybinding settings window.
episodes.instructor_claim: PureRef is ideal for managing multiple reference images outside Blender, allowing always-on-top overlays, copy-pasting from Photoshop, instant cropping with C, and horizontal/vertical flipping.
episodes.interpretation: Using an external floating canvas tool decouples project moodboards from 3D scene files, reducing viewport clutter and scene performance overhead.
episodes.hypothesis: Overlay reference software reduces context-switching latency compared to switching application windows or populating the 3D scene with dozens of image planes.
episodes.concrete_action: Press Ctrl+C in image editor, press Ctrl+V in PureRef, press Ctrl+Shift+A to lock Always-On-Top, hold C and drag mouse to crop image, press Alt+Shift+H to flip image horizontally, right-click -> Settings -> Key Bindings.
episodes.reason: Demonstrate high-efficiency reference manipulation and organizational techniques using dedicated reference software.
episodes.failure_or_warning: Overloading a 3D scene file with numerous high-resolution image planes can impair viewport performance and clutter outliners.
episodes.transferable_principle: Utilize dedicated floating reference software (PureRef) set to 'Always on Top' for flexible moodboard management across 3D applications.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: The instructor opens a web browser to pureref.com, demonstrates where to download the stand-alone program for Windows, Mac, and Linux, notes donation options, and closes with channel credits.
episodes.instructor_claim: PureRef is a standalone tool for Windows, Mac, and Linux available at pureref.com with free or donation-based download options.
episodes.interpretation: PureRef is an accessible cross-platform reference tool suitable for digital artist workflows.
episodes.concrete_action: Navigate to pureref.com and demonstrate download selection options.
episodes.reason: Direct viewers to the source of the reference management application.
episodes.transferable_principle: Leverage cross-platform standalone utilities to standardize reference workflows across operating environments.

contradiction_handling: Instructor demonstrates intentional error (perspective plane import) vs correct method (orthographic view import) to resolve camera projection misalignment.
iterative_research_triggers: When orthographic geometry alone is insufficient to capture 3D form, switch to multi-angle moodboard references.
principles: Always switch to a locked orthographic view before importing image planes intended for orthographic modeling alignment in Blender.
Use dedicated external reference tools like PureRef set to 'Always on Top' for moodboards and auxiliary references to avoid cluttering 3D scene data.
Crop, rotate, and flip reference images dynamically to inspect reverse angles or isolate specific details without destructive image editing.
limitations: PureRef keybindings demonstrated are specific to PureRef software version features.
Viewport image plane performance may depend on Blender viewport shading settings and image resolution.
claims_requiring_external_verification: PureRef software availability, platform support, and pricing/donation model at pureref.com.
proposed_experiments: Compare modeling speed and viewport render performance when using 10 embedded image planes in Blender versus 10 images organized in PureRef on a single monitor setup.
